summary: A neder that compares food to something the Torah already forbids, like pig meat, does not work. But a neder against something the person himself does, like sleeping, does work.

chunks.en: And these nedarim do not work; the thing stays permitted:
chunks.st: And these are
chunks.stMore: the vows in which the one who takes the vow attempts to create a prohibition on an item by associating it with an item in an ineffective manner, rendering the vow void and leaving the item

chunks.en: "What I eat of yours is chullin,"
chunks.st: permitted: If one says: That which I will eat of yours will be non-sacred [ḥullin];

words.note: Plain food that is not holy.

chunks.en: "like pig meat,"
chunks.st: or: That which I will eat of yours will be like pig meat;

chunks.en: "like avodah zarah,"
chunks.st: or: Like an object of idol worship;

chunks.en: "like the skins of animals used for avodah zarah,"
chunks.st: or: Like the hides of animal offerings whose hearts were removed

chunks.en: "like neveilos," "like treifos,"
chunks.st: as a form of idol worship, and it is therefore prohibited to derive benefit from those animals; or: Like animal carcasses and animals with a wound that will cause them to die within twelve months [tereifot];

chunks.en: "like sheratzim," "like crawling creatures,"
chunks.st: or: Like non-kosher repugnant creatures and non-kosher creeping animals;

words.note: Small creatures that are not kosher.

chunks.en: "like the challah of Aharon, or his terumah,"
chunks.st: or: Like the ḥalla of Aaron, the first priest, or like his teruma;

chunks.en: it is permitted.
chunks.st: in all these cases, the food is permitted.
chunks.stMore: Although none of these items may be eaten, they are forbidden by Torah law, not by means of a vow. Therefore, it is impossible to extend their prohibition to other items by means of a vow that associates them with those items.

chunks.en: If a man says to his wife,
chunks.st: With regard to a man who says to his wife:

chunks.en: "You are to me like my mother,"
chunks.st: You are hereby to me like my mother,
chunks.stMore: i.e., deriving benefit from you should be forbidden to me like engaging in sexual intercourse with my mother, dissolution

chunks.en: the Rabbis find him another reason to undo his neder,
chunks.explain: A Rabbi undoes it, but uses a different reason.
chunks.st: is broached with him by suggesting a different extenuation,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a halakhic authority suggests other, extenuating circumstances that enable the dissolution of the vow. Although this vow does not take effect either, as engaging in sexual intercourse with one’s mother is prohibited by Torah law, by rabbinic law this is treated like an actual vow and requires dissolution by a halakhic authority, so

chunks.en: so that he does not take nedarim lightly.
chunks.st: that he will not take genuine vows lightly.

chunks.en: "Konam, that I will not sleep,"
chunks.st: With regard to one who says: Sleeping is forbidden for me as if it were an offering [konam],

chunks.en: "that I will not talk,"
chunks.st: thereby prohibiting himself from sleeping; or: Speaking is konam for me;

chunks.en: "that I will not walk,"
chunks.st: or: Walking is konam for me;

chunks.en: If a man says to his wife,
chunks.st: or one who says to his wife:

chunks.en: "Konam, that I will not be close with you,"
chunks.st: Engaging in sexual intercourse with you is konam for me,

chunks.en: he must keep his word, as the Torah says, "He shall not break his word."
chunks.st: if he violates the vow he is in violation of the prohibition “He shall not profane his word”

chunks.en: If he says, "A shevuah that I will not sleep,"
chunks.st: (Numbers 30:3). If one says: I take an oath that I will not sleep,

chunks.en: "that I will not talk,"
chunks.st: or: That I will not speak,

chunks.en: "that I will not walk," it is forbidden.
chunks.st: or: That I will not walk, this activity is prohibited to him.

summary: Saying "korban" the wrong way does not make a neder, but a shevuah works even then. A shevuah can't stop someone from doing a mitzvah, but a neder can.
stIntro: As taught earlier (10a), one of the primary methods of taking a vow is by invoking an offering. The mishna provides several examples where invoking the term korban is not effective. If one says:

chunks.en: "Korban, I will not eat of yours,"
chunks.st: An offering [korban] that I will not eat of yours,

chunks.en: "Korban, what I eat of yours,"
chunks.st: or: This offering [ha korban] that I will eat of yours,

chunks.en: "Not korban, I will not eat of yours,"
chunks.st: or: That which I will not eat of yours is not an offering [la korban],

chunks.en: it is permitted.
chunks.st: the food is permitted.

chunks.en: "A shevuah, I will not eat of yours,"
chunks.st: If one says: An oath that I will not eat of yours,

chunks.en: "A shevuah, what I eat of yours,"
chunks.st: or: This is an oath that I will eat of yours [she’okhal lekha],

chunks.en: "Not a shevuah, I will not eat of yours,"
chunks.st: or: Not an oath that I will not eat of yours,

chunks.en: it is forbidden. This is a way a shevuah is stronger than a neder.
chunks.st: the food is forbidden. This rule, that oaths can render actions, which do not have actual substance, either prohibited or obligatory, is a stringency of oaths vis-à-vis vows,

chunks.en: And a neder is stronger than a shevuah in another way.
chunks.st: which do not take effect with regard to matters that do not have actual substance. And there is also a stringency of vows vis-à-vis oaths.

chunks.en: How? If he said,
chunks.st: How so? With regard to one who said:

chunks.en: "Konam is the sukkah that I make,"
chunks.st: Making a sukka is konam for me,

chunks.en: "the lulav that I take,"
chunks.st: or: Taking a lulav is konam for me,

chunks.en: "the tefillin that I put on,"
chunks.st: or: Donning phylacteries is konam for me,

chunks.en: with a neder, it is forbidden;
chunks.st: in the case of vows, the items are rendered forbidden,

chunks.en: with a shevuah, it is permitted,
chunks.st: and he may not perform the mitzva until the vow is dissolved. However, in the case of similar oaths, these items are permitted,

chunks.en: because a shevuah cannot be made to break a mitzvah.
chunks.explain: A neder makes the thing forbidden; a shevuah is about the person.
chunks.st: as one cannot take an oath to transgress the mitzvot.

summary: A second neder on the same thing still counts, but a second shevuah on the same thing does not add anything.

chunks.en: A neder can take hold on top of a neder,
chunks.st: There is a vow within a vow.
chunks.stMore: It is possible to impose an additional prohibition, by means of a vow, on an item that is already forbidden by means of a vow.

chunks.en: but a shevuah cannot take hold on top of a shevuah.
chunks.st: But there is no oath within an oath.
chunks.stMore: If one takes an oath twice with regard to the same action, the second oath does not take effect.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד, אָמַר הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר אִם אֹכַל,
chunks.en: How? If he said, "I am a nazir if I eat,"
chunks.st: How so? If one said: I am hereby a nazirite if I eat,

chunks.en: "I am a nazir if I eat,"
chunks.st: and then repeated: I am hereby a nazirite if I eat, and

chunks.he: וְאָכַל, חַיָּב עַל כָּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת.
chunks.en: and he ate, he must keep both.
chunks.explain: He must be a nazir two times.
chunks.st: then he ate, he is obligated to observe naziriteship for thirty days for each and every one

chunks.en: "A shevuah that I will not eat,"
chunks.st: of the vows, as both vows took effect. However, if he said: I hereby take an oath that I will not eat,

chunks.en: "A shevuah that I will not eat,"
chunks.st: and repeated: I hereby take an oath that I will not eat, and

chunks.en: and he ate, he is only guilty one time.
chunks.st: then he ate, he is liable to bring an offering for only one violation of an oath.

summary: A neder that is not clear is treated strictly, but if the person explains it, we follow his explanation in a lenient way. The mishnah gives examples, and tells how people in Yehudah and the Galil spoke differently.

chunks.en: An unclear neder is treated strictly,
chunks.st: Unspecified vows are treated stringently,

chunks.en: but when he explains it, it is treated leniently.
chunks.st: but their specification, if specification is necessary, is treated leniently.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד, אָמַר הֲרֵי עָלַי כְּבָשָׂר מָלִיחַ,
chunks.en: How? If he said, "This is to me like salted meat,"

summary: Someone who made a neder and then says he meant something silly, so it never counted. Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue about how to deal with him.

chunks.en: If he made a neder with "cherem" and said,
chunks.st: One who took a vow by associating an item with a dedication [ḥerem],

chunks.he: לֹא נָדַרְתִּי אֶלָּא בְחֶרְמוֹ שֶׁל יָם.
chunks.en: "I only meant a fishing net."
chunks.explain: A fishing net is also called "cherem."
chunks.st: saying: This item is hereby forbidden to me like an item dedicated to the Temple, and then said: I took a vow only with the intention that it would be like a sea net [ḥermo shel yam] that is used to catch fish;

chunks.en: Or with "korban," and he said,
chunks.st: or one who took a vow by associating an item with an offering, and then said:

chunks.he: לֹא נָדַרְתִּי אֶלָּא בְקָרְבָּנוֹת שֶׁל מְלָכִים.
chunks.en: "I only meant presents for kings."
chunks.st: I took a vow only with reference to offerings to kings,

chunks.en: "I myself am a korban,"
chunks.st: i.e., a gift for a king, not an offering to God. Or one who said: I am hereby an offering myself [atzmi], and

chunks.he: וְאָמַר, לֹא נָדַרְתִּי אֶלָּא בְעֶצֶם שֶׁהִנַּחְתִּי
chunks.en: and he said, "I only meant a bone that I put aside

chunks.st: then said: I took a vow only with reference to a bone [etzem] that I set aside

chunks.en: for myself to make nedarim with."
chunks.st: for myself to vow with,
